about: Declarations the pre-migration sources carried when the integrator archived them (task tu-retire-legacy-src, 2026-09-12). tools/header_harvest.py replays them beside config/header-promoted.json, so the shared headers carry exactly what the accepted records declared and config/header-canon.json decisions that name one of these files stay resolvable. Each record is the declaration verbatim with the provenance the harvest had given it, plus the sha256 of the archived file and where it went. Since task tu-header-layout (2026-09-12) the replayed declarations are emitted into the published per-TU layout - include/shared.h and include/<unit>/<tu>.h - rather than into include/xeno/<domain>/{types,functions}.h; `relocated_headers` records where the generated files that used to carry them went.

declarations.doc:
/*
 * SIF RPC end callback for the RSSD work area: clears flag bit 3, copies the
 * 32-byte receive record into RssdWork, reports a status (-1 on a nonzero
 * result, else flag bit 5) through the registered one-shot completion
 * callback, then signals the waiting thread's semaphore.
 *
 * It runs from the SIF RPC interrupt context, so it ends with the
 * ee-interrupt-handler-return primitive (docs/ps2-capabilities.md): `sync.l`
 * orders every earlier load/store, including the iSignalSema effects, before
 * `ei` re-enables interrupts on the way out.
 */
declarations.name: RssdSifRpcCallback

declarations.canon: typedef struct RssdRpcResponse { unsigned short _unmodeled_00; short result; int _unmodeled_04[7]; } RssdRpcResponse
declarations.doc:
/*
 * The 32-byte SIF RPC receive record copied into RssdWork.response.
 *
 * Evidence from RssdSifRpcCallback (main:0x00240188):
 * - +0x02 is a signed halfword (lh v0,130(a2), a2 = &RssdWork, so
 *   response+2): nonzero reports the -1 (error) status.
 * - The record is copied as a whole with unaligned doubleword pairs
 *   (ldl/ldr -> sdl/sdr, four of them): its type is not 8-byte aligned.
 * - After the copy the compiler reloads RssdWork.flags (lw v0,0(a2) before
 *   the sra/andi), i.e. the copied record may alias an `int` object under
 *   GCC's type-based aliasing. The words after the two halfwords are
 *   therefore `int`-typed; their meaning is not evidenced by this function,
 *   so they stay an explicit unmodeled word span rather than named fields.
 */
declarations.name: RssdRpcResponse

declarations.canon: typedef struct RssdWorkFlags { int flags; unsigned char _unmodeled_004[0x24]; void (*complete_callback)(int status, RssdRpcResponse *response, void *arg); void *callback_arg; unsigned char _unmodeled_030[0x04]; RssdRpcResponse *response_source; unsigned char _unmodeled_038[0x48]; RssdRpcResponse response; unsigned char _unmodeled_0a0[0x114]; int sema_id; unsigned char _unmodeled_1b8[0x48]; } RssdWorkFlags
declarations.doc:
/*
 * RssdWork is the RSSD RPC / background-wave work area, main:0x004aa080,
 * ELF symbol size 0x200 bytes. The accepted RssdWorkFlags in
 * xeno/core/types.h (from RssdBackgroundNextWave, main:0x0023ff28) only
 * carries the leading `flags` word; this function evidences more of the same
 * object, so the type is extended here under the same tag and leading field
 * (see result.json header_divergence). Bytes this allocation does not access
 * stay explicit unmodeled spans.
 */
declarations.name: RssdWorkFlags
declarations.text:
typedef struct RssdWorkFlags {
    int flags;                            /* +0x000: bit 3 cleared on RPC completion; bit 5 is the success status */
    unsigned char _unmodeled_004[0x24];   /* +0x004..0x027 */
    void (*complete_callback)(int status, RssdRpcResponse *response,
                              void *arg); /* +0x028: one-shot, cleared after use */
    void *callback_arg;                   /* +0x02c: third complete_callback argument */
    unsigned char _unmodeled_030[0x04];   /* +0x030..0x033 */
    RssdRpcResponse *response_source;     /* +0x034: SIF RPC receive buffer */
    unsigned char _unmodeled_038[0x48];   /* +0x038..0x07f */
    RssdRpcResponse response;             /* +0x080..0x09f: copy of *response_source */
    unsigned char _unmodeled_0a0[0x114];  /* +0x0a0..0x1b3 (+0x1ac: thread id, see RssdBackgroundNextWave) */
    int sema_id;                          /* +0x1b4: signalled when the RPC completes */
    unsigned char _unmodeled_1b8[0x48];   /* +0x1b8..0x1ff */
} RssdWorkFlags;

declarations.doc:
/*
 * PARTIAL ACCESSED VIEW up to GameLoopState+0x29f62 (explicit limitation):
 * The full GameLoopState object is 0x2a030 bytes at 0x338680 (nm). Only
 * these offsets are evidenced by the three pinned bodies at
 * 0x00244d20/0x00244e28/0x00244f60 and modeled here:
 *  +0x0c kind u16 (sh/lhu; else-branch sh a0,12(s0)),
 *  +0x10 flags u32 (lw/sw; | 0x80000000 and & ~1),
 *  +0x28 camera_callback (lw 40(s0); null-checked then jalr),
 *  +0x29f40 status u8 (lbu/sb via lui 0x3 + addu + -24768),
 *  +0x29f50 pause_vector 16B Quadword (por + sq 8016(v1) with
 *   v1 = 0x28000 + base; base 0x338680 and offset 0x29f50 16B-aligned),
 *  +0x29f60 saved_kind u16 (lhu/sh; Pause gate compares to 2/3).
 * Spans named _unmodeled_* are opaque sizing bytes never accessed by these
 * bodies, kept only to position the evidenced high offsets for exact
 * codegen. They carry no semantic claim and are not complete-object
 * recovery; the remainder of the 0x2a030-byte object beyond 0x29f62 is
 * unmodeled. The TI store is a typed Quadword zero assignment, not VU/COP2
 * or general wide arithmetic.
 */
declarations.name: GameLoopStateLayout

declarations.doc:

 * 16-byte quadword-aligned vector storage. GameModeDebugMenu clears it
 * through the union's quad member; the wrapping union (rather than a bare
 * Quadword field) matters for the schedule: GCC gives a store through a
 * union member alias set 0, so after reload the quad store conflicts with
 * the following saved_kind load (their addresses use different base
 * registers), which orders the resume block exactly as in the original.
 * Receipt (CP-0151, config/compiler-patterns.json): with a bare Quadword
 * pause_vector, charged form 01 of attempt-bab27253d193 first differs at
 * 0x00245bd0 (the flags lw issues before `lui a0,0x2`); the union forms
 * (that attempt's 02/03, attempt-161337e2d5b2 form 02) are exact. Review
 * core-cc-20260911-b11 re-checked the bare form on this 176-byte packet
 * (review/diag-debugmenu-bare-quadword): same first difference.
 * Only the quad member is accessed in this TU; no other view of the
 * storage is evidenced here.
 */
declarations.name: QuadVector

/*
 * Return-type caveat (independent review 2026-09-10): `long` is a proven
 * zero-extra-instruction codegen lever blocking ee-gcc2.96 -O2 sibling-call
 * (`int`/`void`/int-temp all sibcall to the 24B `j` form; `long` keeps the
 * 32B `jal` form; `unsigned char`/`short` add truncation). `void` vs
 * predicate `int` vs `long` dispose semantics are unproven from callers/data:
 * no direct `jal SCENE_dispose` callers in SLUS_204.69, JNI_isInstanceOf
 * returns int 0/1 (see SCENE_start predicate use), and the original forwards
 * a0/v0 unchanged with gp-loaded classJava_xeno_Scene. For 0/1 values
 * int/long are indistinguishable (upper already zero). No cleaner pure-C
 * hypothesis exists in evidence.
 */
declarations.name: SCENE_dispose

declarations.doc:

 * Stores the menu ids of the occupied attack slots, stopping at the first
 * empty slot, and returns how many were stored.
 *
 * The original loop is not rotated: both exits test at the top of every
 * iteration, including the first one. GCC 2.96 rotates for(;;)/while loops
 * whose body breaks out (and then folds the first slot_index < 3 test); the
 * do { } while (1) spelling keeps the tests in place. The slot's party id is
 * read again for the call, as in the original, which keeps slot++ after the
 * empty-slot test instead of in the halfword load's delay.
 */
declarations.name: PartyAttackerGet

/*
 * PartyTimeLimitCheck (main 0x002b6868, 88 B): clamps an accumulated
 * party-time record shaped like XglClock (the same day/hour/minute/second
 * breakdown xglClockUInt2DayTime writes) to a maximum of 5 days, 3 hours,
 * 59 minutes and 59 seconds.
 *
 * Evidence: PartyTimeUpDate (0x002b6954) refreshes the static party-time
 * record at 0x00491818 with xglClockUInt2DayTime/xglClockDayTime2UInt (an
 * 8-byte ldl/ldr -> sdl/sdr copy) and then calls this function; SeisanTimeEx
 * (0x0029fc44) builds a matching stack record with
 * xglClockUInt2DayTime(sp, quotient) and passes the same record on to
 * PartyTimeDispChange. Both callers discard the returned flag.
 *
 * Only day/hour/minute/second are read or written; status, month and year
 * are never accessed by this function.
 */
declarations.name: PartyTimeLimitCheck

declarations.doc:
/*
 * These are external file-backed witnesses, not candidate-emitted data.
 *
 * ov12:0x00a53008, 12 bytes, SHA-256
 * 0af24906f973437c43cba57232d069ee26beaf4b983824fe0f61727f74d8ee74
 * contains the assertion expression "pMgr != NIL".
 * ov12:0x00a53018, 25 bytes, SHA-256
 * 7337a7a7d9fd799db6b03292e71e8e7304fb41b1c04131c24e14bde7270d8d58
 * contains the source filename "../rg_singleton_id.euc.c".
 * ov12:0x00a53068, 29 bytes, SHA-256
 * 9a9bf18448e6f0547d21b210171dcdd394fa5bd943802154800e3e7ea5b65fc3
 * contains the range expression "0 <= eID && eID < RG_SID_MAX".
 */

relocated_headers.about: The generated pre-migration shared headers. They are cited by the `headers` list of accepted config/units records, which is retained acceptance evidence and is never rewritten, so this map says where each file went when task tu-header-layout replaced the layout. The declarations themselves live on in include/shared.h, include/<unit>/<tu>.h or the consuming TU's own src/<unit>/<tu>.h.
